title: Isaiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 51 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 51.

questions.question: Who are the people addressed in Isaiah 51:1?
options: Ye that follow after righteousness and seek the LORD
The kings and princes of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Ye that follow after righteousness and seek the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:1 specifically says, 'Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD.'

questions.question: To whom does the LORD ask the people to look in Isaiah 51:2?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:2 instructs to 'Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you.'

questions.question: What will the LORD do for Zion according to Isaiah 51:3?
options: Comfort all her waste places and make her wilderness like Eden
Destroy her enemies and exile her people
Make her a land of gold and silver
questions.correctAnswer: Comfort all her waste places and make her wilderness like Eden
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 states, 'For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:4, what will proceed from the LORD?
options: A law and judgment as a light to the people
A flood to cleanse the earth
questions.correctAnswer: A law and judgment as a light to the people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:4 says, 'for a law shall proceed from me, and I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:5 say is near and has gone forth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:5 states, 'My righteousness is near; my salvation is gone forth.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:6 say will happen to the heavens and the earth?
options: Heavens shall vanish like smoke and the earth wax old like a garment
Heavens shall endure forever and the earth shall never fail
Heavens shall be fixed and the earth shall remain unshaken
Heavens shall darken and the earth shall split
questions.correctAnswer: Heavens shall vanish like smoke and the earth wax old like a garment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:6 says, 'the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment.'

questions.question: Who are told not to fear the reproach of men in Isaiah 51:7?
options: Ye that know righteousness and have my law in your heart
questions.correctAnswer: Ye that know righteousness and have my law in your heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:7 instructs, 'Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear ye not the reproach of men.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:8, what will consume those who do not have the LORD's righteousness?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:8 says, 'For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:3 promises that the wilderness will be made like a garden of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 states, 'he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:6 teaches that the LORD's salvation will be temporary and eventually abolished.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:6 says, 'my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 51:1, the people are told to look unto the rock whence they were hewn.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:1 instructs, 'look unto the rock whence ye are hewn.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:7 encourages the people to fear the revilings of men.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:7 says, 'fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 51, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Lift up your eyes to the heavens
Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:1 is the first instruction: 'Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness.' The other instructions come in later verses.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:5, on whom shall the isles wait and trust?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:5 states, 'the isles shall wait upon me, and on mine arm shall they trust.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:4, what will the LORD make his judgment to be?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:4 says, 'I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people.'

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 51 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:9, what ancient deeds is the 'arm of the LORD' called to awake and put on strength for?
options: Cutting Rahab and wounding the dragon
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting Rahab and wounding the dragon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:9 specifically calls the 'arm of the LORD' to awake as in the ancient days, recalling the acts of cutting Rahab and wounding the dragon, symbolizing God's power over chaos. This connects to the power described in 51:15 where God divided the sea and made a way for the redeemed.

questions.question: What significant event is described in Isaiah 51:10 that relates to God's deliverance?
options: Drying the sea and making a way for the ransomed to pass
Calling Abraham alone and blessing him
questions.correctAnswer: Drying the sea and making a way for the ransomed to pass
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:10 emphasizes God's power in delivering His people by drying the sea and making a path for the ransomed to cross, which relates to God's historical salvation acts and reassures the redeemed's future return in 51:11.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 51:11 describe the mood of the redeemed of the LORD when they return to Zion?
options: With singing, everlasting joy, gladness, and sorrow fleeing away
questions.correctAnswer: With singing, everlasting joy, gladness, and sorrow fleeing away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:11 vividly depicts the redeemed returning joyfully with singing, everlasting joy, and gladness, while sorrow and mourning flee away. This joy contrasts with the previous suffering mentioned in verses 17-20 and is grounded in God's comforting presence described in 51:12.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:12, what reason is given to not fear mortal men?
options: Because God comforts and mortal men are like grass that will wither
questions.correctAnswer: Because God comforts and mortal men are like grass that will wither
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:12 contrasts God's eternal comfort with the temporary nature of men, described as grass that withers. This teaches believers to trust God's enduring care rather than fear mortal threats, linking to the reassurance in 51:11 of joy replacing mourning.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:13 suggest about those who fear the oppressor's fury daily?
options: They forget the LORD who created the heavens and earth
They are justified in their fear
They are protected by the oppressor
questions.correctAnswer: They forget the LORD who created the heavens and earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:13 rebukes those who fear the oppressor's fury daily as forgetting the LORD the Maker of heaven and earth, implying that faith and remembrance of God’s sovereignty should overcome fear, connecting to the comfort promised in 51:12 and deliverance in 51:14.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:14, what is the hope for the captive exile?
options: To be loosed and not die in the pit or fail in bread
questions.correctAnswer: To be loosed and not die in the pit or fail in bread
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:14 expresses the hope and promise that the captive exile will hasten to be loosed from captivity and will not die in the pit nor lack bread, symbolizing God's provision and deliverance, which ties to God's power to divide the sea in 51:15.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 51:15 identify the LORD in relation to the sea?
options: As the one who divided the sea, whose waves roared
As the one who created the fish
As the one who sank the great ships
As the one who controls the rain
questions.correctAnswer: As the one who divided the sea, whose waves roared
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:15 highlights God's mighty acts by identifying Him as the LORD who divided the sea and whose waves roared, emphasizing His power over nature and deliverance for His people, connecting to the deliverance imagery in 51:9-10.

questions.question: What purpose does God state for putting His words in the mouth of His servant in Isaiah 51:16?
options: To plant the heavens, lay the earth's foundations, and declare Zion as His people
To prophesy doom on the nations
To teach the laws of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: To plant the heavens, lay the earth's foundations, and declare Zion as His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:16 explains that God placed His words in the servant's mouth to establish creation's order and to proclaim Zion as His people, showing divine authority and care, which supports the comfort and restoration themes in 51:11-13.

questions.question: What biblical virtue does Isaiah 51:12 teach about facing fear and suffering?
options: Trust in God's comfort rather than fear mortal men
Avoid all conflict to stay safe
Rely on human strength to overcome
Ignore suffering and pretend it doesn't exist
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God's comfort rather than fear mortal men
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:12 teaches believers to rely on God's comfort and not fear mortal men, who are temporary like grass, encouraging faith over fear in times of suffering. This complements the joyful return described in 51:11 and the rebuke of fear in 51:13.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 51:11, what happens when the redeemed return to Zion?
options: They come with singing and everlasting joy, and sorrow flees away
They seek revenge on their oppressors
questions.correctAnswer: They come with singing and everlasting joy, and sorrow flees away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:11 promises that the redeemed will return joyfully with singing and everlasting joy, with sorrow and mourning fleeing, symbolizing restoration and hope after trials, which contrasts the suffering in verses 17-20.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:13 encourages believers to fear the oppressor continually because he is ready to destroy them.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:13 questions why believers fear the oppressor continually, implying they should not because God, the Maker of heaven and earth, is sovereign. The verse challenges fear, encouraging trust in God’s power instead.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:14 offers hope that the captive exile will be freed and sustained.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:14 clearly states that the captive exile will hasten to be loosed and will not die in the pit or lack bread, offering hope and assurance of God’s deliverance and provision.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:15 identifies the LORD as powerless over the sea and waves.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:15 explicitly states that the LORD divided the sea and that His waves roared, demonstrating His sovereign power over nature, which contradicts the idea of being powerless.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:16 illustrate about the relationship between God's words and His people?
options: God places His words in the servant's mouth and covers them, declaring Zion as His people
God hides His words to keep them secret
God's words are irrelevant to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God places His words in the servant's mouth and covers them, declaring Zion as His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:16 shows God's intimate involvement by putting His words in the servant's mouth and covering him, symbolizing protection and authority, while declaring Zion as His people, indicating covenant relationship and care.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 51:11 and 51:12 together teach about faith and hope in God’s salvation?
options: The redeemed will return with joy because God comforts and believers should not fear mortal men
Believers should only fear mortal men and avoid God
Joy and comfort come from human strength alone
Sorrow and mourning will always dominate
questions.correctAnswer: The redeemed will return with joy because God comforts and believers should not fear mortal men
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:11 promises joyful return of the redeemed, and 51:12 encourages believers not to fear mortal men because God comforts them, teaching that faith in God's salvation brings hope and joy despite adversity.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 51.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:17, what has Jerusalem drunk at the hand of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:17 states that Jerusalem has drunk 'the cup of his fury' at the hand of the LORD, emphasizing divine judgment upon the city.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:18, what is lacking among the sons Jerusalem has brought forth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:18 explains that there is none to guide or take the hand of the sons Jerusalem has brought forth, indicating abandonment and lack of support.

questions.question: What two calamities are mentioned in Isaiah 51:19 as having come upon Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:19 lists 'desolation and destruction' along with famine and sword as the calamities that have befallen Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:20, the sons of Jerusalem are compared to what animal caught in a net?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:20 uses the simile of a wild bull caught in a net to describe the fainted sons lying at the head of the streets, illustrating their helplessness.

questions.question: Isaiah 51:21 describes the afflicted as being drunken. What is the cause of their drunkenness?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:21 explicitly says the afflicted and drunken are not drunk with wine, indicating their condition is spiritual or emotional rather than physical intoxication.

questions.question: What action does the LORD declare He has taken concerning the 'cup of trembling' in Isaiah 51:22?
options: Taken it out of Jerusalem's hand
questions.correctAnswer: Taken it out of Jerusalem's hand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:22 states that the LORD has taken the cup of trembling out of Jerusalem's hand, symbolizing the removal of judgment or suffering.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:23, into whose hands will the cup of wrath be put?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:23 says the cup will be put into the hands of those who afflict Jerusalem, transferring the judgment to her oppressors.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God comforting Zion and transforming her wilderness like Eden, as stated in Isaiah 51:3?
questions.explanation: Psalm 147:3 speaks of God healing the brokenhearted and binding up their wounds, a theme closely related to Isaiah 51:3's promise of comfort and restoration to Zion.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Isaiah 51:9-10 when calling on the 'arm of the LORD' to awake and recalling ancient deeds?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:9-10 uses personification by addressing the 'arm of the LORD' as if it were a person capable of awakening and performing mighty deeds.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:16, what metaphor is used to describe God's protection over Zion?
options: Covered thee in the shadow of mine hand
Built a wall of fire around thee
Set a flaming sword before thee
Placed a crown upon thy head
questions.correctAnswer: Covered thee in the shadow of mine hand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:16 uses the metaphor of God's protective shadow of His hand over Zion, symbolizing care and shelter.

questions.question: What is the original Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'salvation' in Isaiah 51:6, which is said to be forever?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word often translated as 'salvation' is 'Yeshua,' which means deliverance or rescue, as reflected in Isaiah 51:6's promise of eternal salvation.

questions.question: Which New Testament book references the fulfillment of the promise of everlasting joy and the removal of sorrow mentioned in Isaiah 51:11?
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 echoes Isaiah 51:11 by describing a time when God will wipe away all tears, and there will be no more death or sorrow, fulfilling the promise of everlasting joy.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:12, whom does God identify Himself as to comfort His people?
options: I, even I, am he that comforteth you
questions.correctAnswer: I, even I, am he that comforteth you
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:12 clearly states 'I, even I, am he that comforteth you,' emphasizing God's personal commitment to comfort His people.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:13 criticizes the people for forgetting the LORD their maker who stretched forth the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:13 rebukes the people for forgetting the LORD who created the heavens and earth, highlighting their misplaced fear of oppressors.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 51:15 describes the LORD as the one who divided the sea and whose waves roared.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:15 declares that the LORD is the God who divided the sea and whose waves roared, affirming His power over nature.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 51 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:1 encourage the followers of righteousness to do?
options: Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn
questions.correctAnswer: Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:1 calls the followers of righteousness to look unto their origins as a means of encouragement and remembrance of God's faithfulness.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:3, what transformation does the LORD promise for Zion?
options: Her wilderness will become like Eden
questions.correctAnswer: Her wilderness will become like Eden
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 discusses God's promise to comfort Zion and transform her desolation into a flourishing state, likening it to Eden.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:5, what shall the isles do regarding the arm of the LORD?
options: They shall seek it in vain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:5 indicates that the isles will wait upon and trust in the arm of the LORD, highlighting reliance on God's strength.

questions.question: What assurance does Isaiah 51:6 provide about God's salvation?
options: It will be for a short season
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:6 emphasizes the eternal nature of God's salvation, contrasting it with the temporality of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What does God encourage the people to remember in Isaiah 51:12?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 51:12, God reassures His people that He is the one who comforts them, reminding them not to fear human threats.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 51:15?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:15 reveals God's sovereignty as He declares His control over nature and the elements, demonstrating His power.

questions.question: In Isaiah 51:9, what does the speaker call upon to awaken?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:9 calls for the arm of the LORD to awake, invoking God’s past actions as a source of strength and encouragement.

questions.question: What two conditions does Isaiah 51:19 mention that have come upon Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:19 outlines the dire conditions of desolation and destruction that have befallen Zion, emphasizing her plight.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:23 say God will do with the cup of trembling?
options: He will take it from them
He will give it to their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will give it to their enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:23 states that God will place the cup of trembling into the hands of those who have afflicted His people, indicating divine justice.

questions.question: What role does Isaiah 51:4 assign to God's law among His people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:4 describes God's law as a guiding light for the people, providing direction and clarity in their lives.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:8 assert about God's righteousness in comparison to earthly things?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:8 emphasizes the eternal nature of God's righteousness, contrasting it with the temporary nature of earthly matters.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 51:18, what is the condition of Zion's children?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:18 highlights the despondency among Zion's children, indicating a lack of guidance and hope in their situation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:11 promise the redeemed of the LORD will experience?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:11 promises that the redeemed will come to Zion with singing and everlasting joy, highlighting God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 51:13 describe the people's fear of the oppressor?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:13 illustrates the people's continual fear of the oppressor, suggesting a lack of trust in God as their protector.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 51:2 highlight as a key figure in the ancestry of Israel?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 51:2 emphasizes Abraham as a foundational figure for Israel, reminding them of God's covenant and blessings.
